item.title: 伊朗总统表示美国备忘录是摆脱僵局的最佳途径以及其他中东新闻
item.description:
Iran’s president on Sunday defended amemorandum of understandingwith the United States as the best way out of astalled warwhile the new head of the Islamic Republic’s top security body took a more defiant stance, warning of retaliation if neighbors joinU.S. threatsto further sanction Tehran.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Monday is expected to announce new measures against Iran after the U.S. vowed to impose an “unprecedented” level of economic warfare and isolation. Also Monday, Pakistan’s army chief planned to travel to Tehran, Iranian media reported, as mediators try to revive talks.
Meanwhile, violence continued in the occupiedWest Bank, and a hospital said an Israeli airstrike in Gaza killed a child.
Here’s a look at the latest developments in the Iran war and the wider Middle East on Sunday. Full coverage can befound here.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian defended the memorandum of understanding signed in mid-June as the best way to move beyond a situation of “neither war nor peace.”
“There is not a single provision in this agreement that amounts to capitulation,” Pezeshkian said in a speech published by state-run IRNA early Sunday. “The supreme leader sets the policies, and we will follow that path.”
The memorandum of understanding opened a 60-day period for talks aimed at ending the war and reaching an accord on Iran’snuclear program. That period ended last week with no signs of compromise, especially on the crucial issue of reopening the Strait of Hormuz, vital to global shipping.
Pezeshkian said the country can’t attract investment in this stalled phase. Nearly six months after the war began,Iran’s economyis suffering under sanctions and a U.S.naval blockade.
The hard-line leader of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, in his most extensive public comments since being named to the post this month, warned Tehran’s neighbors against joining the new U.S. effort to hurt Iran’s economy and said they would be considered enemies.
“If (Trump) wants to do something, we will retaliate in a seismic manner,” Mohsen Rezaei told the state broadcaster in an interview that aired late Saturday. He said Iran would target oil-shipping routes out of the Persian Gulf — alternatives to the Strait of Hormuz — if neighbors join in.
Rezaei, a former Revolutionary Guard commander and military adviser to Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, was part of senior appointments widely seen as hardening Tehran’s political and military stance.
There were no confirmed attacks in the Strait of Hormuz over the past 48 hours, a multinational coalition overseen by the U.S. Navy said Sunday, with shipping traffic still at reduced levels.
Pakistani Field MarshalAsim Munirwill lead a delegation to Tehran on Monday, Iranian state television reported, citing Iran’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson, Esmail Baghaei.
Two regional officials said the visit was part of Islamabad’s efforts to de-escalate tensions between the United States and Iran and urge them to return to the negotiating table. The officials spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to discuss the matter publicly.
The Iranian judiciary’s Mizan news agency reported the latest execution connected to nationwide protests early this year, saying Majid Adineh was arrested Jan. 9 in Mohammadshahr, west of Tehran.
The judiciary said forensic examinations indicated the handgun found on him had been fired on Jan. 8 and 9. Mizan said Adineh had joined the unrest following calls by groups opposed to Iran’s government and alleged that he had received training from groups outside the country.
A Revolutionary Court in Karaj convicted Adineh under Iran’s law imposing harsher penalties for espionage and cooperation with hostile states. Mizan said the verdict accused him of carrying out operations on behalf of Israel, the United States and groups Iran considers hostile.
Police arrested a 16-year-old boy from the Israeli settlement of Avigayil in the beating of a 61-year-old Palestinian man. Saeed Muhammad Ibrahim Rabah was struck with a pipe outside his home in the occupied West Bank, a year after he lost a leg after being shot by a settler.
Rabah told The Associated Press that two settlers arrived at his home in Khirbet al-Rakeez on Saturday afternoon. One struck him on his back when he approached, Rabah said. He called the violence an effort to make families leave.
“We will remain, no matter what happens,” he said after filing a police report. “This is our land and this is our homeland, and we must protect it.”
Separately, the health ministry in the West Bank said a 14-year-old in the Askar refugee camp in Nablus was shot dead by Israeli forces, who did not immediately comment. The uncle of Islam Maher Ajouri, Nehad Ajouri, called the shooting indiscriminate.
And Israel’s military said it had detained a suspect in a stabbing attack that wounded a 24-year-old Israeli man in the area of al-Auja in the West Bank. Israel’s emergency services said the man was taken to a hospital in moderate condition.
Four-year-old Mohammed Taha died after an Israeli airstrike hit a house in central Gaza on Sunday, hospital authorities said. The strike in Zawaida also wounded at least five other people, including a child, according to the Al-Aqsa Martyrs hospital, which received the casualties.
The military later said it struck and killed a Hamas commander in central Gaza. Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital confirmed that the man named in the statement, Ismail Abu Ful, was killed.
An Israeli strike in southern Gaza wounded at least seven people, including three children, according to health officials at Nasser Hospital. The military did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Also, Defense Minister Israel Katz in a statement said he instructed the military to “act immediately and forcefully” to prevent launches of balloons, kites or drones from Gaza toward nearby Israeli communities.
“We view every launch as an act of war in every respect,” he said.
Before the Oct. 7, 2023, attack by Hamas-led militants on Israel — when 1,200 people were killed and 251 taken hostage —burning kites and balloonswere sent from Gaza into southern Israel, causing fires and other damage.
While the heaviest fighting has subsided since a fragile ceasefire in theIsrael-Hamas wartook hold in October, Israeli forces have carried out repeated airstrikes, killing more than 1,280 Palestinians, according to health officials in Gaza.
The Gaza Health Ministry, part of the Hamas-led government, maintains detailed casualty records that are seen as generally reliable by U.N. agencies and independent experts. It doesn’t give a breakdown of civilians and militants.

item.title: 卡尼对经济胁迫发出警告。现在特朗普正在考验加拿大总理
item.description:
TORONTO (AP) — Mark Carney drew international attention as Canada’s prime minister by warning thatmiddle powersmust resisteconomic coercionby more powerful countries. NowPresident Donald Trumpis putting that warning to the test with sweepingnew tariffsthat could show how much economic pain Canada can absorb.
Tensions escalatedlate Friday when Canadawalked away from negotiationsafter Carney concluded the United States was demanding too much in exchange for tariff relief. The U.S. imposed 50% duties Saturday on about $20 billion worth of Canadian goods, and Carney announced dollar-for-dollar retaliation beginning Sept. 8.
Carney is doing what many other American allies have so far avoided: risking economic pain rather than yielding to tariff pressure.
For Carney, the showdown is the clearest test yet of his argument thatmiddle powersmust stand up to economic pressure from great powers such as the United States and China, even when it comes at a cost. Canada’s response could show how countries navigate a world in which long-standing alliances offer less protection and economic ties themselves become sources of leverage.
It could also shape how Carney is viewed at home and abroad, and how other U.S. allies respond to the Republican president.
The trade dispute also has become a test of sovereignty.
Carney said Washington introduced language in the final hours of negotiations that would have restricted Canada’s ability to make trade deals with other countries. He said that demand was “unacceptable” and “a question of sovereignty.”
British Columbia Premier David Eby said accepting such a condition would have reduced Canada “to the economic equivalent of the 51st state” — a statusTrump has mused about often.
Carney’s message resonated in January when he addressed the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland, as Europe braced forTrump’s threats over Greenlandand new tariffs.
Carney said the international order was undergoing “a rupture, not a transition.” He argued that sovereignty would depend increasingly on a country’s ability to “withstand pressure” and warned that middle powers negotiating alone with great powers do so from weakness.
Trump responded a day later by stressing Canada’s dependence on the United States. “Canada lives because of the United States,” he said. “Remember that, Mark, the next time you make your statements.”
The president has repeatedly talked about making Canada the 51st U.S. state and dismissed the allies’ border as artificial. On Sunday, Trump returned to that theme, writing on Truth Social that “Canada wants the benefits of being a State, without being one!!!” and accusing Canada of charging U.S. farmers “massive amounts” of tariffs for years. “No more!!!” he wrote.
Seven months since Davos, Canada has become a test case for the world Carney described.
“Our government understood, before many, that America would transform all its commercial relationships,” Carney said Saturday. He accused Washington of using “economic integration as a weapon” and said its “signature was written in pencil.”
Historian Robert Bothwell said Canada is uniquely vulnerable to U.S. pressure.
“No country is more exposed than Canada,” Bothwell said. “Other countries have to fear American misbehavior, but none as much as Canada.”
Bothwell said success ultimately means Canada retaining its independence “in the face of Trump’s desire to subordinate it and absorb it.” He said Carney “sees that very well.”
But Canada’s dependence on the U.S. market makes that difficult.
Nearly three-quarters of Canadian exports go to the United States, whose economy is roughly 10 times larger. Canada can sign new trade agreements, but replacing customers and supply chains built around the enormous U.S. market over decades is considerably harder.
Carney acknowledged retaliation would “raise costs and reduce choice for Canadians.”
U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer rejected Canada’s account of the breakdown in talks, saying Ottawa introduced new demands and backed away from commitments even after Washington offered to reduce tariffs on steel, autos, lumber and other goods.
He said the United States was moving ahead with additional measures in response to Canada’s retaliation, raising the prospect of further escalation.
The European Union prepared retaliatory tariffs against the United States last year but repeatedly suspended them while negotiating with Washington.
Nelson Wiseman, a professor emeritus of political science at the University of Toronto, said Canada is providing the biggest test yet of whether Carney’s strategy can work and whether resistance by one middle power could change the calculations of others.
“Will there be a domino effect? We’ll see,” Wiseman said.
Ian Bremmer, president of the Eurasia Group, said Americans underestimate how angry Canadians are with the Trump administration.
“Taking a hard line in response to U.S. policy perceived as predatory — even with major economic cost to Canada — is popular among most Canadians,” he said in a social media post.
That anger again spilled into sports over the weekend. Fans in Vancouver and Montreal booed the U.S. national anthem before Major League Soccer matches Saturday, echoing similar scenes early in the trade war last year.
Manitoba Premier Wab Kinew said Canadians should be prepared for a prolonged confrontation and that Trump could emerge weaker after the U.S. midterm elections in November.
“He’s got two more years left in office. We should be prepared to duke it out for two years, and then hopefully, sanity will return,” Kinew said.
Carney has framed the confrontation as a test of whether Canada can preserve its independence under U.S. pressure.
“Last spring, I warned that America is trying to break us so that they can own us,” Carney said Saturday. “And I promised: ‘That will never, ever happen.’ We are keeping that promise.”

item.title: 北京机器人赛中国仿人机器人打破人类100米短跑和跳高纪录
item.description:
北京（美联社）——周六，类似奥运会的世界人形机器人运动会在北京开幕，中国人形机器人打破了人类创下的纪录，其中包括打破尤塞恩·博尔特的 100 米短跑世界纪录。
组织者称，有超过2000个人形机器人参加了此次活动。
2026 年 8 月 22 日星期六，在北京举行的世界人形机器人运动会开幕式上，机器人敲鼓表演。（美联社照片/Achmad Ibrahim）
为期五天的比赛现已进入第二年，随着与美国的技术竞赛日趋白热化，中国在先进机器人领域的快速进步展现了中国在先进机器人领域的快速进步，共有51个小项和1000多个比赛项目，其中包括跑步、乒乓球和足球。
比赛在为 2022 年冬奥会建造的国家速滑馆举行，比赛在北京举办 2026 年世界机器人大会的同一周开幕，会上各企业展示了约 3,000 种产品，其中包括人形机器人。
世界上大部分人形机器人都是中国制造的。美国加强了对该国机器人的审查。
上个月，美国联邦通信委员会宣布禁止进口新型外国制造的人形机器人。美国联邦通信委员会(FCC)以国家安全为由，采取了针对中国的举措。五角大楼最近还将中国领先的人形机器人制造商之一 Unitree 添加到其认为与中国军方有联系的公司名单中。北京对这些指控进行了回击。
在周六的机器人比赛开幕式上，主办方和机器人制造商表示，中国人形机器人打破了人类世界纪录，数百台人形机器人列队行进赛场，展示了大规模的同步协调。
在100米短跑比赛中，仿人机器人取得了9.39秒的成绩，打破了牙买加运动员博尔特在2009年创下的9.58秒的人类纪录。
在立定跳高比赛中，人形机器人达到了2.88米，远高于去年第一届奥运会上人形机器人0.95米的最好成绩。它超越了古巴选手哈维尔·索托马约尔在1993年创下的2.45米的人类跳高纪录。
这两款机器人均来自北京的 X-Humanoid。
开幕前，中国智能手机公司荣耀的仿人机器人在试赛中以9.32秒的成绩完成了百米冲刺，该公司表示，峰值速度为每秒14.5米。
2026 年 8 月 22 日星期六，在北京举行的世界人形机器人运动会开幕式上，机器人参加 100 米比赛。（美联社照片/Achmad Ibrahim）
尽管如此，专家表示，人形机器人仍然主要用于演示、表演和研究——至少目前如此——而且实现大规模现实世界部署仍需要时间。
机器人比赛的一些观众表示，他们对人形机器人快速提高的能力感到兴奋。
北京居民、教育工作者李艳峰说，人形机器人正在“迅速发展”。
“一开始，我不太接受人工智能。我什至有点抗拒它，因为它有可能取代或取代人类，”她说。“但现在我看到这种发展势不可挡，我决定过来看看。”
“这些运动对于人类来说是再平常不过的事了，但现在机器人也能做这些了，我觉得太神奇了。”另一位观众杨尚正说。
2026 年 8 月 22 日星期六，在北京举行的世界人形机器人运动会开幕式上，观众般的机器人在表演。（美联社照片/Achmad Ibrahim）
和儿子一起观看比赛的刘涛表示，他希望看到“中国目前最好的机器人”。
今年的机器人比赛——组织者称有 16 个国家参加，其中包括德国、日本和美国——还包括举重和拔河等其他项目。
陈浩谦从香港报道。Olivia 张和刘铮在北京为本报告做出了贡献。

item.title: 联邦法官撤销特朗普暂停处理 75 个国家移民签证的政策
item.description:
纽约一名联邦法官撤销了特朗普政府暂停处理来自 75 个国家签证的政策，其中包括阿富汗、伊朗、俄罗斯和索马里，特朗普政府认为这些国家的国民可能需要在美国提供公共援助。
前总统乔·拜登任命的美国地区法官珍妮特·巴尔加斯周五撤销了这项政策，称其“违反法律且超出法定权力”。
法官裁定，国务卿马可·卢比奥发布这项政策超越了他的职权，该政策要求“在没有任何法律依据的情况下拒绝向符合条件的申请人发放签证”，从而“违反”了《移民和国籍法》。
巴尔加斯表示，这项政策还破坏了国会将领事官员置于任何签证决定最前线的要求。
她写道：“国会赋予这些官员专属权力和自由裁量权，根据对法规中规定的具体和详细标准的审查来确定移民是否有资格获得签证。”“该政策明确禁止根据申请人的国籍签发移民签证，代表着对这一法定计划的直接废除。”
该政策受到两个非营利组织以及 11 个人的质疑，其中 6 人的家庭成员被拒绝签证。其余五人在国外，并已提交“基于就业的申请”来美国。
“我们欢迎这一裁决，因为从本质上讲，此案是为了让家庭团聚，”CLICNIC 的执行董事安娜·加拉格尔 (Anna Gallagher) 说。CLICNIC 是一家全国性非营利组织，为移民法律服务提供商网络提供培训、资源和支持，也是原告之一。
她在一份声明中说：“天主教的社会教义要求我们维护每个人的尊严，并承认家庭是社会的基础。”“这一决定肯定了这些价值观和法治，让家庭再次朝着团聚迈进。”
另一原告是位于哈莱姆区的非营利组织非洲社区。其一位领导人称这一裁决是“法治的巨大胜利”。
负责政策和宣传的副执行主任戴安娜·科纳特在一份声明中表示：“这项非法的种族主义禁令造成了不可估量的伤害，残酷地使家人和亲人分离。”“今天，我们很高兴地告诉我们的社区成员：这项禁令已不再存在。”
唐纳德·特朗普总统实施了越来越多的移民和旅行禁令，主要针对来自非洲、亚洲和拉丁美洲的人。美国国务院周六表示，特朗普政府正在“通过维护签证申请人的最高筛选和审查标准来保护美国人民”，并且不会对未决诉讼发表评论。
该政策发布时，国务院表示已指示领事官员停止来自 75 个国家的移民签证申请，这是根据 11 月份一项更广泛的命令，该命令收紧了对可能成为“公共负担”的潜在移民的规定。美国国务院根据经济顾问委员会的数据表示，超过 30% 的来自这些国家的移民家庭获得了某种形式的公共援助。
发给所有美国大使馆和领事馆的另一份通知称，非移民签证申请人也应接受“全面审查和筛选”，以确定他们可能在美国寻求公共福利的可能性。
美联社获得了该电报的副本，电报多次指出，申请人必须证明他们在美国期间不会申请公共福利，而怀疑申请人可能申请的领事官员应要求他们填写一份表格，证明其财务真实性。
该裁决是法院颠覆特朗普移民议程的最新例子。六月，一名联邦法官推翻了特朗普政府的一项政策，该政策使来自数十个国家的移民更难进入和留在美国，影响到庇护、工作许可、绿卡和公民身份申请等要素。该法官表示，这项政策使无数移民的生活“陷入不确定的法律困境”，并指责美国公民和移民服务局无视法律。

item.title: 随着风力增强，热带风暴莫克向夏威夷推进
item.description:
火奴鲁鲁（美联社）——热带风暴莫克周六向夏威夷推进，可能给大岛带来更多强降雨和强阵风，当地居民仍在应对飓风拉拉造成的严重洪水和破坏性大风的后果。
2026 年 8 月 17 日星期一，飓风拉拉带来大雨后，夏威夷纳阿莱胡的一条道路被泥土冲毁。（艾娜·阿卡姆，美联社）
莫克于周五在太平洋形成，位于希洛东南约 425 英里（680 公里）处，以 12 英里/小时（19 公里/小时）的速度向西北偏西移动。国家飓风中心表示，最大持续风速约为 50 英里/小时（85 公里/小时）。
与飓风拉拉一样，预计大岛将首当其冲地受到莫克降雨和强风的影响，因为它从周六晚间到周日早些时候直接袭击以南。
火奴鲁鲁国家气象局气象学家凯西·奥斯旺特表示，预计莫克将在周二早些时候继续在岛屿附近向西移动。
奥斯万特说：“影响仍然会存在，特别是对大岛的迎风面和东南面，但影响可能比我们在拉拉身上看到的要有限一些。”
拉拉砍倒了树木，将建筑物从地基上冲走，损坏了道路和桥梁，并使道路被泥土和岩石覆盖。据报道有两起与风暴有关的死亡事件。
2026 年 8 月 17 日星期一，夏威夷州纳阿勒胡飓风拉拉过后，Ka’u 汽车修理店被一片废墟包围。（Stephen Lam/《旧金山纪事报》，美联社）
奥斯万特说，预计大岛东南部和迎风面的周末降雨量为 5 至 10 英寸（13 至 25 厘米），偏远地区可达 15 英寸（38 厘米）。岛链其他地区预计降雨量为 1 至 2 英寸（2 至 5 厘米），但毛伊岛东部部分地区降雨量可能高达 4 英寸（10 厘米）。
目前没有有效的沿海监视或警告，但敦促人们密切监视风暴的进展。该中心表示，降雨有可能引发危险的离岸流、危及生命的洪水和泥石流，特别是在陡峭地区和地面仍然饱和的地方。
据气象部门称，大岛东北海岸的拉拉总降雨量最大，达 43.54 英寸（1.1 米）。据 poweroutage.us 称，夏威夷大岛仍有 8,000 多名客户断电。
2026 年 8 月 16 日星期日，在夏威夷山景城，恶劣天气系统袭击该地区后，一名青少年涉水穿过受损道路被冲毁的水池。（斯蒂芬·林 / 旧金山纪事报，美联社）
夏威夷州州长乔什·格林和其他州官员在莫克之前举行了新闻发布会，敦促人们做好准备，补充食品、药品和其他必需品。
住在大岛东侧凯奥的教师蒂芙尼·爱德华兹·亨特 (Tiffany Edwards Hunt) 表示，一想到社区里的降雨量增多，洪水变成了河流，“空气中肯定弥漫着紧张气氛”。
美联社底特律撰稿人亚历克斯·圣约翰对此作出了贡献。

item.title: Buc-ee 连锁店因争夺一家迷你超市的海狸标志而引发俄亥俄州强烈抗议
item.description:
BEAVERCREEK, Ohio (AP) — A lip-licking alligator, a smiling moose and a hat-wearing bear are among the many cartoon animals to have found themselves in the crosshairs ofBuc-ee’s, the popular Texas convenience store chain that has a penchant for protecting its buck-toothed beaver.
But now Buc-ee’s has set off a Buckeye backlash across Ohio and beyond after taking on a beaver in the city of Beavercreek.
It’s yet another Buc-ee’s Ltd.trademark infringement lawsuit. Supporters of Beaver’s Mini Mart have attacked Buc-ee’s online and boycotted the stores, and the mini mart’s home city passed a resolution making the beaver an official part of its history. British comedianJohn Oliverhas even weighed in on the kerfuffle.
On an episode of “Last Week Tonight with John Oliver,” the comedian detailed Buc-ee’s aggressive history of trademark lawsuits targeting various woodland creatures and launched a website hawking merchandise bearing a knockoff “Buc-off” logo and a squirrel mascot named Mr. Nutterbutter. On X, #boycottbucees trended.
Buc-ee’s sued Beaver’s Mini Mart in late July, four months after the chain known for its extensive food offerings and massive restrooms opened its first Ohio store less than a half-hour’s drive away.
Buc-ee’s argues the shop’s beaver logo too closely resembles the convenience store giant’s branded Buc-ee (“Bucky”) beaver. The Texas-based company asked for a jury trial in federal court in Ohio.
Beaver’s Mini Mart occupies a long, low building with a shingle roof at a suburban intersection. In contrast, the new 74,000-square-foot (6,875-square-meter) Buc-ee’s off Interstate 70 near Dayton has more than 100 gas pumps, 24 electric vehicle chargers and 700 parking spaces. A second Ohio store has been approved to open in 2028.
While preparing to enter the state in February, Buc-ee’s sued the northern Ohio holding company for Mickey Mart gas stations, arguing its Mickey the Moose logo could be confused with Buc-ee. (The company’s response: “A moose is not a beaver.”)
The Buc-ee’s beaver logo features the face of a beaver with prominent buck teeth wearing a red ball cap against a yellow backdrop. The Beaver’s Mini Mart mascot is a full beaver, unclothed, waving and smiling against a white background.
Customers have been critical of Buc-ee’s decision to target the much smaller store.
“I love Buc-ee’s, but I don’t plan on going back until they start making better business decisions,” Austin Collins, 32, a project manager from Fairborn, said outside Beaver’s, where he was making his first visit to protest the lawsuit.
He called targeting a beaver-named business in Beavercreek “a little spiteful.” License plates from three states were visible in the parking lot.
Buc-ee’s has defended the lawsuit as protective of its valuable trademark. In a statement on its website, the company said it first learned of Beaver’s Mini Mart when its owner, Vic Boparai,filed a trade name registrationon Oct. 23.
The small business, incorporated in 2017, changed its name from Hanes Road Carryout to Beaver’s Mini Mart in January 2025, according to the paperwork. That was about four months after Buc-ee’s broke ground near Dayton. Recognizing a conflict, the company said it repeatedly attempted to reach Boparai without success, so it was forced to sue.
Boparai has since issued a statement of his own, though without addressing the company’s concerns nor the merits of the lawsuit.
“We want to say thank you to the community and the entire country for supporting us and our business,” he said. “We are overwhelmed by your support for our business and other small businesses everywhere.”
The Associated Press has been unable to reach Boparai at Beaver’s Mini Mart or by calling the store.
Beavercreek City Council responded to the dust-up by passing a resolution Aug. 10 making the beaver a permanent and official part of its 200-plus-year history. Bucky the Beaver, mascot of the Beavercreek Local Schools, visited the meeting ahead of the unanimous vote.
On social media, images lampooning the fight are rampant. One showed the Ohio State University football mascot, Brutus Buckeye, tackling Buc-ee the beaver.
Support has taken other forms, too. One was a GoFundMe campaign aimed at assuring that costs associated with the lawsuit don’t put Beaver’s Mini Mart out of business, as has happened to other establishments Buc-ee’s sued. It had raised at least $69,000.
The mini mart gave permission to The Original Goodie Shop bakery in Upper Arlington to use its logo on a signature cookie, with $1 from each one sold going to support Beaver’s legal fees. Cake, Hope & Love, a Beavercreek bakery, also is offering cookies adorned with buck-toothed beavers that urge shopping local.
Other Dayton-area businesses — including a Lego store and a root beer shop — temporarily altered their logos to include beavers in a show of solidarity. Dozens of businesses in Beavercreek already incorporate the city name or word beaver in their names.
Republican Ohio Gov. Mike DeWine, who attended and praised the grand opening of the Dayton-area Buc-ee’s store in April, described the lawsuit as “absurd.”
“It is Beavercreek, for heaven’s sake,” the governor told reporters.

item.title: 特朗普敦促法院驳回BBC在诽谤案中获取其家人记录的请求
item.description:
华盛顿（美联社）——唐纳德·特朗普总统敦促联邦法官驳回 BBC 请求法院帮助获取三名家庭成员的证词和文件的请求，以回应他针对英国广播公司提起的价值 100 亿美元的诽谤诉讼。
这位共和党总统的私人律师在周五的法庭文件中辩称，BBC 正试图通过向女儿伊万卡·特朗普、女婿贾里德·库什纳和儿子小唐纳德·特朗普发出传票来获得对特朗普的“政治影响力”。
迈阿密的美国地区法官杰弗里·昆茨没有立即对这一纠纷做出裁决。
被特朗普提名为法官的昆茨不到一周前从另一位法官手中继承了总统的诉讼。法院文件没有立即具体说明案件重新分配的原因。前任法官已定下二月的审判日期。
据总统的律师称，今年 5 月，一名为 BBC 工作的传票员试图在伊万卡·特朗普和库什纳的住所向他们送达传票，但遇到了特勤局特工，特勤局特工表示他们无权接受传票。他们表示，几天后，流程服务器还访问了纽约的特朗普大厦，但未能为小唐纳德·特朗普提供服务。
在上周提交的法庭文件中，该广播公司请求法院允许通过挂号信而不是亲自向特朗普的家人送达传票。
特朗普于 12 月提起诉讼，指控 BBC 对他 2021 年 1 月 6 日在白宫附近发表的演讲的部分内容进行了欺骗性编辑，当时特朗普的一群支持者袭击了国会大厦，以阻止国会认可民主党人乔·拜登战胜特朗普。该诉讼称，BBC 将特朗普演讲的不同部分拼接在一起，故意歪曲他的言论。
该诉讼称，BBC 在 2024 年总统大选前一周播出了这部纪录片，“公然试图干涉和影响”选举结果，损害特朗普的利益。
特朗普的律师写道：“BBC 动议所寻求的救济不能与该动议所基于的充满政治色彩的发现运动分开，而该运动已被本法院裁定为不当过于宽泛。”
这是我们的 AP Ground Game 时事通讯。您可以在下面订阅，我们每周会向您发送 3 次电子邮件。
本网站受 reCAPTCHA 和 Google 隐私政策和服务条款的保护。
BBC 已就误导性编辑向特朗普道歉，但否认诽谤他。

item.title: 皮特·布蒂吉格返回南卡罗来纳州，考虑再次竞选白宫
item.description:
ORANGEBURG, S.C. (AP) — The last timePete Buttigiegwas giving a political speech in South Carolina, it was to mark a distant finish in the state’s primary that effectivelyended his campaign for president.
Returning this weekend as he mulls a second run for the White House, Buttigieg set out to reintroduce himself to the state and the Black voters he struggled to win in 2020. The results were encouraging.
There was a standing ovation in a Black church in South Carolina when Buttigieg was credited for helping bring millions of federal dollars to the area for a project as President Joe Biden’s transportation secretary. A second ovation came as Buttigieg gave a speech warning of a country in “big trouble” while laying out his own vision for what should come next.
“There is no such thing as again in real life. The only way out is through,” Buttigieg told the crowd of more than 200 people at an NAACP Freedom Fund Dinner. “If we recognize and embrace a future that is different from the past, we will do better.”
The warm applause was a markedly different reception than six years ago, when a fourth-place showing in South Carolina helped derail Buttigieg’s presidential campaign while exposing his failure to connect with Black voters. The state is likely to have an even greater say in his political future asthe first contestin the Democratic presidential primary in 2028.
Starting the election calendar in South Carolina is intended in part to give Black voters a greater voice at the outset of the nominating process. For Buttigieg and other potential contenders, winning the support of this group that makes up a majority of South Carolina’s Democratic electorate is essential.
“You need to demonstrate that you can win Black voters,” said Jaime Harrison, a former Democratic National Committee chair and South Carolina Democratic Party chairman. “If you can’t win Black voters, you can’t be the nominee of our party.”
Buttigieg insists he has made no final decision about whether to run for president again.
“Right now, I’m totally focused on 2026,” he told reporters Saturday.
But his South Carolina trip — a week after visiting another early-voting state, Nevada — had all the trappings of a potential presidential bid.
He raised money Friday in Charleston with Nancy Lacore, a U.S. House candidate trying to flip a Republican-held seat. On Saturday morning, he spoke at a policy conference before traveling to Claflin University, a historically Black university in Orangeburg.
Davina Perry, a third-year student at Claflin, said she came away from Buttigieg’s visit thinking he would be a “good candidate” if he ran.

“Secretary Pete has definitely put himself on my radar for 2028 now, for sure,” Perry said. But, she added, “I do want to see more representation from people who look like me.”
That evening, Buttigieg attended a dinner at a church in Orangeburg, a nearly three-quarters Black city with a deep history in the Civil Rights Movement. The crowd included local NAACP leaders, ministers and elected officials. Buttigieg worked the room, giving hugs and taking photos.
“He is responsible for the Railroad Corner,” said Orangeburg Mayor Michael Butler, referencing a project aimed at revitalizing the city’s downtown that received a $22.7 million federal grant. “Do I need to say any more? We need to stand and welcome the former secretary.”
Buttigieg used the speech that followed to make a broader case about the direction of the country, arguing that Democrats cannot separate Americans’ economic frustrations from a political system he described as increasingly broken.
“I have come to believe that the kitchen table cannot be improved unless we are also reforming the institutional and political floor on which that kitchen table sits.”
For Buttigieg, the weekend offered signs of how much has changed since he came to South Carolina in 2020 as a 38-year-old Indiana mayor asking voters to take a chance on him. He points to what he delivered during four years in Biden’s Cabinet, including specific projects in the state.
But Buttigieg said he also came to South Carolina “to propose something” about the country’s future. Butler, Orangeburg’s mayor, liked what he heard.
“His speech was what you talk about at the kitchen table. How America is going to survive all of this?” Butler said. “He brought hope to us.”
South Carolina Democratic leaders say the close, personal engagement with candidates is exactly what they hoped for. Those involved in the push to make South Carolina first envisioned the living-room conversations and retail politics long associated with Iowa and New Hampshire.
“You got to go listen. You got to go all over the place,” Harrison said. “You have to make meaningful investments. That’s how you win South Carolina.”
Buttigieg is hardly alone in his early trip to the state.
Other potential 2028 contenders, including California Gov. Gavin Newsom, Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear, U.S. Rep. Ro Khanna of California and U.S. Sen. Cory Booker of New Jersey have made trips to the state as what is expected to be a large Democratic field begins to take shape. Former Vice President Kamala Harris already has deep ties in the state.
The electorate they will encounter has changed from 2020, when Biden’s victory in the state resurrected his presidential campaign and put him on a path to ousting Republican President Donald Trump.
Four years later, Trump defeated Harris and returned to the White House, which Black leaders say has significantly hurt their community. Earlier this year, a Supreme Court decision weakened a core provision of the Voting Rights Act, threatening Black political representation across the South.
“We must start our process where democracy must still be fought for, in the full view of the nation,” former interim DNC chair Donna Brazile said in a speech this year advocating for South Carolina to go first.
Buttigieg addressed that anxiety directly Saturday night, describing efforts to weaken the Voting Rights Act as the culmination of a “multidecade effort.” He warned of a broader push “to demolish African American political power.”
Harrison said Buttigieg’s trip this weekend was a “good start,” but that Buttigieg and all the other potential 2028 candidates have a long road ahead to prove themselves to the state’s voters.
“It has to be a good start and then you got to continue,” Harrison said. “It can’t just be, ‘Oh, pop in and then I’m going to pop back out.’”
This story corrects the spelling of the first name of Claflin University student to Davina Perry, from Divina Perry.

item.title: 特朗普挥舞绿旗开始印地赛车比赛，赛车手们在华盛顿的街道上疾驰
item.description:
WASHINGTON (AP) — For once, things were moving fast in the nation’s capital.
Washington was hosting anIndyCar racethrough its streets Sunday, with PresidentDonald Trumpand first lady Melania Trump kicking off the Freedom 250 Grand Prix by leading a slow lap in the presidential limousine through the course. Soon after, the president waved the green flag to start the race and drivers began whipping through downtown, including a stretch along Pennsylvania Avenue not too far from the White House.
“I’m going to make a little circle in a nice, secure car, slightly slower than the ones we’re going to witness, but we’re going to have fun,” Trump said in an interview on Fox shortly before the ride.
The open-wheel race, with cars whizzing past Washington’s monuments at speeds approaching 200 mph,is the latest of Trump’s celebrationsthis year to mark America’s 250th birthday.
Trump’s other events to mark the semiquincentennial of the Declaration of Independence’s signing have includeda UFC fight on the White House lawn, military aircraft flyovers,a massive July Fourth fireworks showon the National Mall and a Great American State Fair thatthe president headlinedafter scores of ’90s-era musical acts dropped out. The events have all had a Trumpian flair, featuring appearances from his friends and the aim of showcasing spectacle, Americana and power.
In this latest case, it was be horsepower.
Sunday included some of Trump’s favorite flourishes. One of his favorite singers, tenor Christopher Macchio, performed, “The Star-Spangled Banner.” A trained bald eagle was dramatically released near the start line, and it swooped and flew overhead before returning to its handler.
There were flyovers of military aircraft, which have boomed over the city during the July Fourth celebrations, among other events. One flyover Sunday involved a formation featuring a B-2 stealth bomber, which Trump frequently boasts about for its role in dropping massive bunker-buster bombs on Iranian nuclear facilities last year.
Air Force One, escorted by four fighter jets, flew overhead as Trump did his lap. The jet was the Qatar-gifted aircraft that the president has been using as Air Force One, which has attracted scrutiny not only for Trump’s acceptance of the luxury gift but because it isnot equippedwith some of the same missile detection and countermeasure systems found on older presidential jets.
The IndyCar race took place Trump has struggled to resolve the war he started nearly six months ago with Iran, a conflict that has driven up gasoline prices and exacerbated worries from officials in his Republican Party that voters in thisNovember’s midterm electionssee the president as distracted and not focused enough on cost-of-living concerns.
Trump in his second term has increasingly seemed to focus on relishing the presidency’s ceremonial aspects. That’s included a healthy dose of visits to sporting events — including an appearance last month at the World Cup final,where he presented the trophy to winner Spainand lingered onstage with the team as its members jumped in a hail of confetti.
From his viewing box, Trump had the honor of waving the green flag to kick off the race.
Before the race, Trump and his wife met and chatted with some of the race drivers. They then took a slow drive through the course in a small motorcade and could be seen waving at the crowd as a Marine Corps band played “Stars and Stripes Forever.”

This site is protected by reCAPTCHA and the GooglePrivacy PolicyandTerms of Serviceapply.
IndyCar series owner Roger Penske, a longtime friend of Trump’s who received thePresidential Medal of Freedomfrom him in 2019, helped lead the effort to bring the race to Washington.
Trump told Fox on Sunday that Penske told him that he had been trying to bring the race to Washington for 20 years.
“When he came to see Trump it got done in about 15 minutes and it’s turned out to be much bigger than we ever even thought possible,” the president said, referring to himself in the third person.
Penske met Trump when he arrived at the course and later joined him in his viewing box, as did the president’s friend and UFC CEO Dana White, who helped put on the fight at the White House in June.
Anexecutive order Trump signed earlier this yearcalling for the Freedom 250 Grand Prix declared that the “cars and drivers inspire awe and respect in all who watch this quintessentially American sport,” and the event will “showcase the majesty of our great city as drivers navigate a track around our iconic national monuments in celebration of America’s 250th birthday.”
“Their beautiful cars are going to make freedom roar. This will be a freedom that’s roaring like never before,” Trump said at the White House earlier this month as he promoted the event.
Bud Denker, president of Penske Corporation and the race’s chair, said that Penske is paying for the “vast majority” of the race, including building the track and road improvements, while the District of Columbia handled some repaving.
Among the changes needed on the city’s streets for the Indycar race was the welding of more than 200 maintenance hole covers to ensure the race cars don’t suck them up off the road.
Sunday’s festivities were also the latest opportunity for Trumpto revel in the way he’s putting his mark on the nation’s capital, includinglarge banners showing his face on government buildings, the construction of a massive White House ballroom, a gold-adorned Oval Office andbotched repairs at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool.

item.title: 跨性别辩论在 Fever 比赛中引发集会，布里安娜·斯图尔特 (Breanna Stewart) 希望有一个安全的空间
item.description:
纽约（美联社）——纽约自由队球星布里安娜·斯图尔特一直将 WNBA 视为一个包容性的地方，为球迷和球员提供安全的空间。最近这一点受到了挑战。
最近，WNBA 一直是关于是否应该允许跨性别女性（出生时被指定为男性，但为了适应自己的性别认同而转变）的辩论的主题。WNBA从来没有出现过这样的球员。尽管联盟的集体谈判协议规定 WNBA 仅限女性参加，但它没有包含有关性别认同或出生性别的更具体的语言。
印第安纳狂热队的索菲·坎宁安 (Sophie Cunningham) 在上个月发布的 ESPN 简介中表示，她反对变性女孩和妇女参加女子和女子运动项目，此后，印第安纳狂热队的索菲·坎宁安 (Sophie Cunningham) 表示，她反对跨性别女孩和妇女参加女子和女子运动项目，这一问题达到了紧要关头，随后，印第安纳狂热队比赛场外出现了小型集会和抗议活动。在周六晚上狂热队对阵纽约自由队之前，举行了两次代表跨性别问题双方的和平集会。自由队以109-102赢得了比赛。
周六上午，斯图尔特对一小​​群记者表示：“知道双方都在举行集会，这表明W党拥有的平台和吸引注意力的噱头只是在继续尝试驾驭我们现有的浪潮。”“我希望今晚来到这里的自由球迷甚至印地球迷能够让这个竞技场成为一个安全的空间。”
坎宁安认为，她的评论所吸引的所有关注都是积极的，因为它为比赛带来了更多粉丝。
“你有很多新球迷，他们不仅会观看比赛，还会来看比赛，看看环境，看看人才，”她在赛前说道。“我认为任何时候你都能吸引更多人关注 W，这是一件很棒的事情，因为这会激励其他可能从未见过这款游戏、听说过这款游戏或参加过游戏的孩子，他们会获得这种体验。所以我绝对认为这是一件非常积极的事情。”
上周日在亚特兰大梦想队和狂热队之间的比赛中，至少三名球迷被 WNBA 安保人员要求遮盖印有变性女性参与女子运动的信息的衬衫。联盟后来表示球迷应该可以自由穿着这些球衣。
斯图尔特特别表示，自由球迷和 WNBA 球迷都会来观看比赛，因为“他们会觉得自己可以以任何身份做自己，我们不想忽视这一点。”
这位自由前锋表示，每个人都有权发表自己的意见，如果这种情况不再被允许，就会出现更大的问题。然而，她表示，不应容忍试图分裂球队和球员的行为。
“如果我们不允许（言论自由），我们需要真正回去看看更多的事情。我认为更重要的是人们试图将我们划分为团队、队友或对手，”她说。“这个联盟具有令人难以置信的包容性，也是我们继续争取和反对的目标。因此，我们不想剥夺这个平台。”
斯图尔特在她的职业生涯中一直是跨性别群体的盟友。去年，当她的一款签名鞋带有哈利波特主题时，她在网上遭到了一些强烈反对。斯图尔特是《哈利·波特》系列书籍和作者 J.K. 所著后续电影的忠实粉丝。罗琳斯因其反变性而受到批评。
斯图尔特已将该鞋的版税捐赠给了 Trevor Project，这是一个针对 LGBTQ+ 青少年的自杀预防和危机干预非营利组织。

item.title: 哈兰德的发型：曼城球星为新赛季剪掉了头发
item.description:
英国曼彻斯特（美联社）——埃尔林·哈兰德著名的飘逸秀发已不复存在。
这位曼城超级巨星为新赛季英超联赛换了一个新发型：周日，在球队对阵伯恩茅斯的揭幕战之前，他的短发在社交媒体上疯传。
这对他没有帮助。这位挪威前锋在曼城2-1战胜阿提哈德球场的比赛中错失了几次绝佳机会。
哈兰德因其长发而成为近年来最容易辨认的体育明星之一。
在哈兰德 YouTube 频道上的一段视频中，兹拉坦·伊布拉希莫维奇询问这位曼城前锋在看到新发型时是否“输了赌注”。
“你现在会更快，还是怎样？”伊布说道。
前曼城主帅瓜迪奥拉对这一发型的反应是：“你很幸运能拥有头发。我很想拥有它！”
哈兰德抵达阿提哈德球场观看伯恩茅斯的比赛时戴着帽子，但在热身时帽子被摘掉了——露出了嗡嗡声。

item.title: 因描绘针对女性的暴力行为而受到批评后，Good Good Golf 下架了视频
item.description:
内容创作者 Good Good Golf 是今年秋季新的 PGA 巡回赛赛事的冠名赞助商，他发布了一段卡拉威发球杆的视频，随后又删除了该视频，视频中一名男子将一名伸手去抓新发球杆的女子推倒在地。
周五晚间，Good Good 和 Callaway 因批评该视频描绘了针对女性的暴力行为而被删除，不过在官方账号将其删除后，该广告的片段仍在社交媒体上流传。
广告中的人物都是 Good Good 的成员——加勒特·克拉克 (Garrett Clark)，他冲过去推了亚历克西斯·米斯特夫斯基 (Alexis Miestowski)，然后在她躺在地上时对她说：“别碰我的新一号木。”
Good Good周六在社交媒体上发表声明道歉说：“我们在自己的渠道上发布了一段视频，该视频最终描绘了与我们作为品牌价值观不符的行为。我们已删除该内容，并真诚地道歉。Good Good始终致力于让高尔夫运动对所有人更具包容性，我们将继续确保这是我们未来的使命。”
Good Good Golf 于 2020 年作为 YouTube 频道推出，现已成为这项运动中最大的内容创作者之一，其中有八名男子和四名女子参加高尔夫和各种挑战赛。它提供电视节目、服装和其他商品。
卡拉威高尔夫 (Callaway Golf) 于 2023 年与 Good Good 合作。
卡拉威高尔夫在一份声明中表示：“我们对发布的内容感到失望，并感谢 Good Good 解决了这个问题。我们期待共同努力，确保高尔夫领域更具包容性。”
PGA 巡回赛在过去几年中一直在拥抱内容创作者，Good Good 今年迈出了一大步，成为了 Good Good 锦标赛的冠名赞助商，该锦标赛是联邦快递杯秋季赛的一部分，将于 11 月 12 日至 15 日在德克萨斯州奥斯汀举行。
美巡赛在一份声明中表示：“美巡赛相信高尔夫运动能够将人们聚集在一起，为所有人创造一个受欢迎的环境。我们不纵容任何形式的暴力行为，并且删除后的视频并不反映我们的价值观或对包容和尊重的承诺。”

item.title: 摩城早期歌曲作家珍妮·布拉德福德·霍布斯 (Janie Bradford Hobbs) 因病在洛杉矶去世，享年 87 岁
item.description:
摩城早期歌曲作家珍妮·布拉德福德·霍布斯 (Janie Bradford Hobbs) 的家人周六表示，她因长期患病在洛杉矶一家医院去世，她曾帮助创作了《Money (That's What I Want)》和《Too Busy Thinking About My Baby》等热门歌曲。她87岁了。
布拉德福德·霍布斯出生于密苏里州查尔斯顿，后来搬到底特律。
20 世纪 50 年代末，她经邻居兼歌手杰基·威尔逊 (Jackie Wilson) 介绍认识了摩城创始人贝里·戈迪 (Berry Gordy)。她于 1958 年加入摩城担任接待员，与公司的许多员工一样，她参与了创意过程，帮助摩城成为音乐行业的巨头。
她和戈迪合写了《金钱（这就是我想要的）》。这首歌由 Barrett Strong 于 1959 年录制，并成为早期热门歌曲。它被披头士乐队翻唱，也成为该乐队的热门歌曲之一。
《Too Busy Thinking About My Baby》首先由 The Temptations 录制，后来成为马文·盖伊 (Marvin Gaye) 的热门歌曲。布拉德福德·霍布斯还为史蒂夫·旺德、The Supremes、Martha & The Vandellas 等人创作了歌曲。
戈迪在一份声明中说：“珍妮从一开始就和我在一起，甚至在摩城还没有出现之前，她将永远在我心中和摩城大家庭中占据一个非常特殊的位置。”
“珍妮是我一直认为摩城家族的特殊群体之一，他们是无名英雄，在人们知道摩城会变成什么样子之前，他们就相信了自己的梦想，”戈迪继续说道。“她是帮助摩城发展成为现在这个样子的人之一。”
布拉德福德·霍布斯后来成为摩城出版公司乔贝特的作家关系主管。离开摩城后，她创办了年度英雄与传奇奖。据她的家人称，这项活动持续了大约 30 年，旨在表彰音乐偶像并颁发奖学金。
她的丈夫沃丁·霍布斯（Wardean Hobbs）去世了。女儿，妮可·霍布斯；儿子兰斯·芬尼；和两个孙子。葬礼尚未完成。

item.title: 《蜘蛛侠》第四周末票房冠军《奥德赛》成为诺兰票房最高的电影
item.description:
《蜘蛛侠：崭新的一天》击败了包括喜剧片、恐怖片、杰森·斯坦森动作片和家庭片在内的一大批新片，在上映第四周保持了票房第一的位置。《奥德赛》也成为克里斯托弗·诺兰有史以来票房最高的电影，无论是国内还是国际。
据电影公司周日估计，今年《奥德赛》仅次于《蜘蛛侠》，美国和加拿大的 4,006 家影院为《蜘蛛侠》增加了 3,900 万美元的票房收入。《蜘蛛侠》目前在北美的票房收入已超过 8.549 亿美元，很快将超越《复仇者联盟：终局之战》，成为有史以来第二高的国内电影票房。目前的纪录保持者是《星球大战：原力觉醒》（9.367 亿美元）。
索尼还推出了周末第二大电影《潜伏：超越》。该系列的第六部电影由 Blumhouse Atomic Monster 制作，在 3,303 家影院上映，票房收入达 2,530 万美元。在国际上，它赚了 3500 万美元。其 1800 万美元的制作预算使其成为该系列中最昂贵的电影。
第三名是《奥德赛》，该片本周早些时候超越了《死侍与金刚狼》，成为有史以来票房最高的 R 级电影。该片在北美影院上映的第六个周末票房收入增加了 1,950 万美元，并继续在 3,000 多个地点上映，使其国内总票房接近 5.391 亿美元。这使得《黑暗骑士》的票房收入突破了 5.349 亿美元——这是诺兰之前的最高纪录——不考虑通货膨胀。在国际方面，它增加了 6800 万美元，主要由中国和韩国推动，使其全球总美元达到 14 亿美元。
其他大牌新人的排名进一步下滑。《叛变》由斯坦森主演，饰演一名被错误指控谋杀其亿万富翁老板的男子，该片在 2,703 个地点上映，票房收入 750 万美元，排名第六。狮门影业发行（收购）的目的是只在院线上映，但在上映前几天，它意外地在 Prime Video 上免费播放了几个小时，然后错误才得到纠正。这个故障可能影响了首映周末的收入，但影片也有一些相当糟糕的评论。
评价更差的是《温泉周末》，这是一部由《宿醉》和《坏妈妈》背后的男人们创作的一部女孩旅行喜剧，由艾拉·菲舍尔、莱斯利·曼、安娜·法瑞丝和米歇尔·布托主演。该公司在 2,009 个地点的收入预计为 310 万美元。据 PostTrak 称，在周末开放门票购买者中，女性约占 84%。《速度与激情》25周年纪念版的重映赚得稍微多一些。
由安德鲁·加菲尔德 (Andrew Garfield) 主演的《遥远的魔法树》(The Magic Faraway Tree) 在 1,611 块银幕上上映，票房收入 140 万美元，超出了前十名。
然而，安东尼·波登 (Anthony Bourdain) 的年轻电影《托尼》(Tony) 仍然表现出色，在 1,652 块银幕上获得了 500 万美元的票房收入。
截至劳动节的夏季门票收入目前在北美已创造了约 44 亿美元的收入，跻身有史以来票房收入最高的四个夏季门票之列。
Rentrak 市场趋势主管保罗·德加拉贝迪安 (Paul Dergarabedian) 表示：“我认为，我们正处于票房历史上最重要、最关键的夏季电影季之一的冲刺阶段。”“我不知道今年夏天如何复制。工作室会尝试的。”
电影院贸易组织 Cinema United 的总裁兼首席执行官迈克尔·奥利里 (Michael O’Leary) 指出，市场上种类繁多的电影为暑期档的上映做出了贡献。他告诉美联社，部分原因是该行业终于从 2023 年好莱坞罢工的影响中恢复过来。
“坦率地说，最令我兴奋的是电影观众的热情，”奥利里说。“当你去剧院时，你会感觉到这一点。在剧院里有一种最近从未有过的能量。”
今年总体也超过了 70 亿美元，比 2025 年增长约 20.4%，但比 2019 年落后约 7.1%。
根据 Rentrak 的数据，随着周一公布的最终国内数据，该清单考虑了美国和加拿大影院周五至周日的预计门票销售情况：
1.《蜘蛛侠：崭新的一天》，3900万美元。
2.《潜伏：超越》，2530万美元。
4.《狗狗巡逻队：恐龙电影》，910万美元。
8.《速度与激情》（25 周年纪念版），310 万美元。
10.《瘴气营的青少年性与死亡》，190万美元。
